Verification command: PIHOLE_DNS_PUBLICATION=$(docker compose -f "$PIHOLE_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --format json | jq -r --arg service "$PIHOLE_SERVICE" '.[] | select(.Service == $service) | (.Publishers // [])[] | select(.TargetPort == 53 and .PublishedPort == 53) | [(.URL // ""), (.PublishedPort | tostring)] | @tsv' | head -n 1) && PIHOLE_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.NetworkMode}}' "$PIHOLE_CONTAINER_ID") && if test -n "$PIHOLE_DNS_PUBLICATION"; then IFS=$'\t' read -r PIHOLE_DNS_HOST PIHOLE_DNS_PORT <<< "$PIHOLE_DNS_PUBLICATION"; case "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" in ''|'0.0.0.0'|'::'|'[::]') PIHOLE_DNS_HOST=127.0.0.1 ;; esac; else test "$PIHOLE_NETWORK_MODE" = host && PIHOLE_DNS_HOST=127.0.0.1 && PIHOLE_DNS_PORT=53; fi && test "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" = 53 && ss -lunt | awk '$5 ~ /:53$/ { found=1 } END { exit !found }' && if command -v dig > /dev/null; then test -n "$(dig @"$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" -p "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" example.com A +short +time=3 +tries=1)"; elif command -v nslookup > /dev/null; then nslookup example.com "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" > /dev/null; else printf '%s\n' 'Install the Debian dnsutils package for dig or provide nslookup, then rerun verification.' >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Runtime metadata supplies a reusable host-side Pi-hole DNS listener from a published port or host networking, a TCP or UDP listener is present on port 53, and a direct query to that discovered listener returns an address for example.com.

If verification fails: Check port publishing or host-network mode in the protected Compose definition, port conflicts, firewall policy, Pi-hole service logs, resolver readiness, and whether dig or nslookup is installed. Do not change DNS configuration merely to make the test pass.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Local DNS is not restored until Pi-hole listens on port 53 and answers a practical resolution query.

sections.heading: 7. Verify administrative interface
paragraphs: Required operator action: Discover a usable Pi-hole administrative endpoint from Docker and Compose metadata, preferring a published host mapping for container port 80 or 443, then host networking, and using a container network address only as a fallback. Verify the administrative path exists without logging in or exposing a password, token, credential, or environment value.

Verification command: PIHOLE_WEB_PUBLICATION=$(docker compose -f "$PIHOLE_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --format json | jq -r --arg service "$PIHOLE_SERVICE" '.[] | select(.Service == $service) | (.Publishers // [])[] | select(.TargetPort == 80 or .TargetPort == 443) | [(.TargetPort | tostring), (.PublishedPort | tostring), (.URL // "")] | @tsv' | sort -n | head -n 1) && PIHOLE_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker inspect --format '{{.HostConfig.NetworkMode}}' "$PIHOLE_CONTAINER_ID") && if test -n "$PIHOLE_WEB_PUBLICATION"; then IFS=$'\t' read -r PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT PIHOLE_WEB_HOST_PORT PIHOLE_WEB_HOST <<< "$PIHOLE_WEB_PUBLICATION"; case "$PIHOLE_WEB_HOST" in ''|'0.0.0.0'|'::'|'[::]') PIHOLE_WEB_HOST=127.0.0.1 ;; esac; PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=$PIHOLE_WEB_HOST; PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT=$PIHOLE_WEB_HOST_PORT; else PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT=$(docker inspect "$PIHOLE_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].Config.ExposedPorts // {} | keys[] | split("/")[0] | select(. == "80" or . == "443")' | sort -n | head -n 1) && test -n "$PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT" && if test "$PIHOLE_NETWORK_MODE" = host; then PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=127.0.0.1; PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT=$PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT; else PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=$(docker inspect "$PIHOLE_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].NetworkSettings.Networks | to_entries[] | .value.IPAddress | select(length > 0)' | head -n 1); PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT=$PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT; fi; fi && test -n "$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST" && test -n "$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT" && if test "$PIHOLE_WEB_TARGET_PORT" = 443; then PIHOLE_ADMIN_URL="https://$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST:$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT/admin/"; PIHOLE_HTTP_STATUS=$(curl --insecure --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' "$PIHOLE_ADMIN_URL"); else PIHOLE_ADMIN_URL="http://$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST:$PIHOLE_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT/admin/"; PIHOLE_HTTP_STATUS=$(curl --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' "$PIHOLE_ADMIN_URL"); fi && grep -Eq '^(2[0-9]{2}|3[0-9]{2}|401|403)$' <<< "$PIHOLE_HTTP_STATUS"

Expected successful result: Docker and Compose metadata supply an endpoint using the first applicable mode—published host port, host networking, or container address fallback—and the unauthenticated /admin/ path returns a 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 401, or 403 response. Published host ports may differ from container ports; 404 and unrelated server responses do not pass.

If verification fails: Check the discovered published mapping, host-network mode, fallback container network attachment, administrative path, web-service logs, and local firewall reachability. A 404 means the administrative endpoint was not proven. Do not reveal or reset the administrative password during this non-mutating availability check.
Blocks recovery: Yes. The operational console must respond before Pi-hole recovery can be validated manually.

sections.heading: 8. Verify upstream DNS functionality
paragraphs: Required operator action: From the recovery host, reuse the Pi-hole listener discovered and validated in step 6 to resolve an external public domain through Pi-hole's restored upstream configuration. Do not require diagnostic utilities inside the application container, hardcode an upstream provider, install packages, or mutate the container.

Verification command: test -n "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" && test "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" = 53 && if command -v dig > /dev/null; then test -n "$(dig @"$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" -p "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" example.com A +short +time=3 +tries=1)"; else nslookup example.com "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" > /dev/null; fi

Expected successful result: A host-side query directed specifically to the discovered Pi-hole listener resolves example.com through Pi-hole's configured upstream path without relying on utilities in the Pi-hole image or naming an upstream provider.

If verification fails: Recheck the step 6 listener, upstream reachability, restored Pi-hole resolver settings through protected evidence, Docker networking, host Internet access, firewall rules, and restricted service logs. Do not install tools in the container or print environment variables, credentials, or tokens while diagnosing.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Pi-hole cannot provide dependable external resolution while its configured upstream path fails.

sections.heading: 9. Complete manual validation
paragraphs: Required operator action: In the responding Pi-hole interface, manually confirm the expected blocklists are loaded, expected local DNS records are present, expected DHCP configuration is restored when Pi-hole provides DHCP, and expected client query activity is visible. Use protected recovery evidence for comparison and do not expose passwords, API tokens, or DNS credentials.

Verification command: printf '%s\n' 'Manual Pi-hole validation required:' '  - expected blocklists loaded' '  - expected local DNS records present' '  - expected DHCP configuration confirmed when Pi-hole provides DHCP' '  - expected client query activity visible'

Expected successful result: The operator records confirmation of all four expected outcomes against protected evidence, marking DHCP explicitly not applicable only when Pi-hole is not the environment's DHCP provider.

If verification fails: Return to protected Pi-hole data restoration, confirm the selected recovery point, inspect application behavior without exposing secrets, and keep every missing list, record, DHCP setting, or expected client query documented as a blocker.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Automatic service checks do not replace manual confirmation of restored operational DNS policy and expected client behavior.

sections.heading: 10. Confirm Pi-hole recovery is complete
paragraphs: Required operator action: Proceed only after steps 1 through 9 pass, including every manual confirmation. Recheck local and upstream resolution, then record that dependable local DNS is restored and later application recovery may continue.

Verification command: test -n "$(docker compose -f "$PIHOLE_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$PIHOLE_SERVICE")" && test -n "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" && test "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" = 53 && if command -v dig > /dev/null; then test -n "$(dig @"$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" -p "$PIHOLE_DNS_PORT" example.com A +short +time=3 +tries=1)"; else nslookup example.com "$PIHOLE_DNS_HOST" > /dev/null; fi && printf '%s\n' 'Pi-hole recovery complete: dependable local DNS has been restored; later application recovery may continue.'

Expected successful result: The Pi-hole service remains running, a host-side external-domain query through the reused Pi-hole listener succeeds, all manual validations are complete, and the command states that dependable local DNS has been restored.

If verification fails: Return to the failed container, local DNS, interface, upstream DNS, persistent-data, network, or manual-validation step. Do not authorize later application recovery while any DNS blocker remains.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Later application recovery must wait until dependable local DNS and required manual Pi-hole state are fully validated.

entries.title: Jellyfin Recovery
entries.summary: Restore Jellyfin application state and verify its separately maintained media library.

sections.heading: 1. Locate the Jellyfin Compose project
paragraphs: Required operator action: Open one dedicated recovery shell and use it through step 10. Discover restored Compose definitions beneath /srv/docker, automatically accept a unique Jellyfin definition and service, and use constrained selection only when multiple service-name or image matches exist. Retain non-secret Compose, mount, network, and publication context without relying on generated container names or displaying environment values.

Verification command: mapfile -t JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES < <(while IFS= read -r candidate; do if docker compose -f "$candidate" config --format json | jq -e '.services | to_entries[] | select(((.key + " " + (.value.image // "")) | ascii_downcase) | contains("jellyfin"))' > /dev/null; then printf '%s
' "$candidate"; fi; done < <(find /srv/docker -type f \( -name 'compose.yml' -o -name 'compose.yaml' -o -name 'docker-compose.yml' -o -name 'docker-compose.yaml' \) -print | sort)) && ((${#JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES[@]})) && if ((${#JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES[@]} == 1)); then JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE=${JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES[0]}; else printf 'Select the protected Jellyfin Compose definition:
'; select JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE in "${JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do test -n "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" && break; done; fi && JELLYFIN_PROJECT_DIR=$(dirname -- "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE") && docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --quiet && JELLYFIN_PROJECT_NAME=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r '.name') && mapfile -t JELLYFIN_SERVICE_CANDIDATES < <(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r '.services | to_entries[] | select(((.key + " " + (.value.image // "")) | ascii_downcase) | contains("jellyfin")) | .key') && ((${#JELLYFIN_SERVICE_CANDIDATES[@]})) && if ((${#JELLYFIN_SERVICE_CANDIDATES[@]} == 1)); then JELLYFIN_SERVICE=${JELLYFIN_SERVICE_CANDIDATES[0]}; else printf 'Select the Jellyfin service from the discovered services:
'; select JELLYFIN_SERVICE in "${JELLYFIN_SERVICE_CANDIDATES[@]}"; do test -n "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" && break; done; fi && JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS" && docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg project "$JELLYFIN_PROJECT_NAME" --arg service "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" '. as $config | ($config.services[$service].volumes // [])[] | . as $mount | [$service, $mount.type, (if $mount.type == "volume" then ($config.volumes[$mount.source].name // ($project + "_" + $mount.source)) else ($mount.source // "") end), $mount.target] | @tsv' > "$JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS" && test -s "$JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS" && printf 'Project: %s
Service: %s
Keep this shell open through step 10.
' "$JELLYFIN_PROJECT_NAME" "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE"

Expected successful result: A restored Compose definition containing Jellyfin is uniquely discovered or selected from valid candidates, validates without starting services, and the same shell retains its project, service, and restricted raw-mount context without revealing secrets.

If verification fails: Confirm the protected Jellyfin project was restored under /srv/docker, verify Compose and jq are available, and compare candidate definitions with protected recovery evidence. Do not use running containers as authoritative recovery evidence or print resolved environment values.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin recovery cannot continue without a valid restored Compose definition, identified service, and declared persistent mounts.

sections.heading: 2. Classify Jellyfin mounts
paragraphs: Required operator action: Classify each resolved mount as protected application state, rebuildable cache/transcode storage, external media, or intentionally non-persistent runtime support. Clear targets are classified automatically. For each ambiguous mount, use protected evidence to select one of those four constrained roles; do not type a path or arbitrary value and do not classify a mount as protected merely because Compose declares it.

Verification command: JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && while IFS=$'	' read -r service type source target; do case "${target,,}" in /config|/config/*) classification=protected-state ;; *cache*|*transcode*|/tmp|/tmp/*) classification=rebuildable ;; /media|/media/*|/movies|/movies/*|/tv|/tv/*|/music|/music/*|/recordings|/recordings/*|/photos|/photos/*|/photographs|/photographs/*) classification=external-media ;; /etc/localtime|/etc/timezone) classification=runtime-support ;; *) case "$source" in /srv/storage|/srv/storage/*) classification=external-media ;; *) printf 'Classify Compose mount source %s at target %s using protected evidence:
' "$source" "$target"; select classification in protected-state rebuildable external-media runtime-support; do case "$classification" in protected-state|rebuildable|external-media|runtime-support) break ;; esac; done ;; esac ;; esac; printf '%s	%s	%s	%s	%s
' "$service" "$type" "$source" "$target" "$classification" >> "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT"; done < "$JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS" && test "$(wc -l < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT")" -eq "$(wc -l < "$JELLYFIN_RAW_MOUNTS")" && ! grep -Eq $'	review-required$' "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && printf 'Restricted completed mount report: %s
' "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT"

Expected successful result: The mode-600 report contains exactly one constrained classification for every Compose-derived mount; protected state, rebuildable storage, external media, and runtime support remain distinct, and no mount remains unresolved or review-required.

If verification fails: Repeat the constrained selection using protected Compose and recovery evidence. Do not expose file contents, enter free-form infrastructure values, or silently treat an ambiguous mount as protected state.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Startup safety cannot be established while a persistent mount's role is ambiguous.

sections.heading: 3. Verify protected Jellyfin application state
paragraphs: Required operator action: Before startup, prove every protected-state bind and named volume exists, is readable, and contains bounded evidence of restored Jellyfin state. Empty protected locations block startup. Verify runtime-support mounts exist and are readable without treating them as application state. Rebuildable storage may be absent but must never be deleted or reset. Do not assume host UID/GID values or container users.

Verification command: jellyfin_state_present() { local type=$1 source=$2 mountpoint; case "$type" in bind) test -d "$source" && test -r "$source" && find "$source" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 3 -print -quit | grep -q . ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 && mountpoint=$(docker volume inspect --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' "$source") && test -n "$mountpoint" && sudo test -d "$mountpoint" && sudo test -r "$mountpoint" && sudo find "$mountpoint" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 3 -print -quit | grep -q . ;; *) false ;; esac; } && JELLYFIN_MISSING_STATE=() && JELLYFIN_MISSING_RUNTIME=() && while IFS=$'	' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) jellyfin_state_present "$type" "$source" || JELLYFIN_MISSING_STATE+=("$type:$source") ;; runtime-support) case "$type" in bind) test -e "$source" && test -r "$source" || JELLYFIN_MISSING_RUNTIME+=("bind:$source") ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 || JELLYFIN_MISSING_RUNTIME+=("volume:$source") ;; esac ;; rebuildable) printf 'Rebuildable storage identified: %s -> %s
' "$source" "$target" ;; esac; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && if ((${#JELLYFIN_MISSING_STATE[@]})); then printf 'Missing or empty protected Jellyfin application state:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${JELLYFIN_MISSING_STATE[@]}" >&2; false; fi && if ((${#JELLYFIN_MISSING_RUNTIME[@]})); then printf 'Unavailable Jellyfin runtime-support mounts:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${JELLYFIN_MISSING_RUNTIME[@]}" >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Every protected configuration, database, user/access setting, library definition, metadata, plugin, and other state location is readable and non-empty by a bounded check; runtime-support mounts are available; rebuildable storage remains distinct and unmodified; no filenames or contents are printed.

If verification fails: Restore every listed missing or empty protected bind or named volume from verified Jellyfin application-state evidence, or restore the listed runtime-support dependency. Do not create, initialize, repair, hash, or fully traverse protected state, and do not let Compose initialize a clean server over an empty location.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin must not start when protected application-state data is absent.

sections.heading: 4. Verify external media storage
paragraphs: Required operator action: Verify every external-media bind is readable and has bounded content evidence. A distinct mounted filesystem, including the expected /srv/storage deployment, passes automatically. When an exact Compose-derived source intentionally resides on the root filesystem, confirm that fact using the constrained protected-evidence choice; do not type a path. Media remains excluded from the protected Docker application backup.

Verification command: JELLYFIN_MEDIA_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_MEDIA_REPORT" && JELLYFIN_ROOT_MEDIA_APPROVED=() && JELLYFIN_MISSING_MEDIA=() && while IFS=$'	' read -r service type source target classification; do if test "$classification" = external-media; then media_mount_target=$(findmnt --noheadings --output TARGET --target "$source" 2> /dev/null | head -n 1); if test "$type" != bind || ! test -d "$source" || ! test -r "$source" || test -z "$media_mount_target" || ! find "$source" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -print -quit | grep -q .; then JELLYFIN_MISSING_MEDIA+=("media:$source"); elif test "$media_mount_target" = /; then printf 'Protected evidence must confirm intentional root-filesystem media source %s at target %s:
' "$source" "$target"; select root_media_decision in 'protected evidence confirms this exact source' 'not confirmed'; do case "$root_media_decision" in 'protected evidence confirms this exact source') JELLYFIN_ROOT_MEDIA_APPROVED+=("$source"); break ;; 'not confirmed') JELLYFIN_MISSING_MEDIA+=("unconfirmed-root-media:$source"); break ;; esac; done; else media_device=$(findmnt --noheadings --output MAJ:MIN --target "$source" | head -n 1); printf '%s	%s	%s
' "$source" "$target" "$media_device" >> "$JELLYFIN_MEDIA_REPORT"; fi; fi; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && if ((${#JELLYFIN_MISSING_MEDIA[@]})); then printf 'Unavailable separately maintained Jellyfin media storage:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${JELLYFIN_MISSING_MEDIA[@]}" >&2; false; fi && jellyfin_media_present() { local type=$1 source=$2 mount_target approved=1; test "$type" = bind && test -d "$source" && test -r "$source" && find "$source" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 2 -print -quit | grep -q . || return 1; mount_target=$(findmnt --noheadings --output TARGET --target "$source" 2> /dev/null | head -n 1); test -n "$mount_target" || return 1; if test "$mount_target" = /; then approved=1; for approved_source in "${JELLYFIN_ROOT_MEDIA_APPROVED[@]}"; do test "$approved_source" = "$source" && approved=0; done; return "$approved"; fi; return 0; } && while IFS=$'	' read -r service type source target classification; do test "$classification" != external-media || jellyfin_media_present "$type" "$source" || exit 1; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT"

Expected successful result: Every external media source is a readable non-empty bind verified by a bounded check; distinct mounts such as /srv/storage pass automatically, while an intentional root-filesystem source passes only after constrained confirmation for that exact Compose-derived path. No media filenames are printed.

If verification fails: Recover or reattach missing media from its separately maintained source, or obtain protected evidence for the exact intentional root-filesystem bind and repeat the constrained choice. Do not create directories, print filenames, traverse the full collection, or claim the Docker backup contains excluded media.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin must not start against missing or accidentally empty media bind paths, and full recovery cannot complete without the expected media library.

sections.heading: 5. Verify required Docker networking
paragraphs: Required operator action: Derive Jellyfin's resolved network_mode. Host mode requires no Compose network entry; none blocks service recovery; service: and container: modes block until the shared namespace dependency is independently restored and verified. For normal Compose networking, verify explicit networks or the genuine project default. Do not fabricate or automatically create networks.

Verification command: JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" && JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" '.services[$service].network_mode // ""') && case "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE" in host) printf '%s
' 'Jellyfin uses host networking; no Compose network entry is required.' ;; none) printf '%s
' 'Jellyfin network_mode none cannot provide the required service endpoint.' >&2; false ;; service:*|container:*) printf 'Jellyfin shares a network namespace through %s; independently restore and verify that dependency.
' "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE" >&2; false ;; '') docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg project "$JELLYFIN_PROJECT_NAME" --arg service "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" '. as $config | ($config.services[$service].networks // {}) as $networks | (if ($networks | length) > 0 then ($networks | keys[]) else "default" end) as $key | ($config.networks[$key].name // ($project + "_" + $key))' > "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; bridge) printf '%s
' bridge > "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; *) printf 'Unsupported Jellyfin network_mode: %s
' "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE" >&2; false ;; esac && JELLYFIN_MISSING_NETWORKS=() && while read -r network; do test -z "$network" || docker network inspect "$network" > /dev/null 2>&1 || JELLYFIN_MISSING_NETWORKS+=("$network"); done < "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" && if ((${#JELLYFIN_MISSING_NETWORKS[@]})); then printf 'Missing required Jellyfin networks:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${JELLYFIN_MISSING_NETWORKS[@]}" >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Host mode passes with an empty report; normal Compose or bridge mode reports and verifies only networks Jellyfin actually uses; disabled, shared, or unsupported namespace modes remain explicit blockers.

If verification fails: Restore each actual network from protected Docker Platform evidence, or independently restore and verify the shared namespace dependency. Do not create networks during verification or rely on generated container names.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin must not start until its resolved networking semantics and actual dependencies are verified.

sections.heading: 6. Start the Jellyfin stack
paragraphs: Required operator action: Immediately recheck protected state, external media, named volumes, resolved network mode, and actual networks, then start only the selected Jellyfin Compose project. Rebuildable mounts may be recreated by Compose, but protected state and media may not. Never use a generated container name.

Verification command: JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS=() && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) jellyfin_state_present "$type" "$source" || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("state:$source") ;; external-media) jellyfin_media_present "$type" "$source" || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("media:$source") ;; runtime-support) case "$type" in bind) test -e "$source" && test -r "$source" || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("runtime:$source") ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("runtime-volume:$source") ;; esac ;; esac; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && JELLYFIN_START_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" '.services[$service].network_mode // ""') && test "$JELLYFIN_START_NETWORK_MODE" = "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE" && case "$JELLYFIN_START_NETWORK_MODE" in host) test ! -s "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("unexpected-host-network-report") ;; ''|bridge) while read -r network; do test -z "$network" || docker network inspect "$network" > /dev/null 2>&1 || JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("network:$network"); done < "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; *) JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS+=("unsupported-network-mode:$JELLYFIN_START_NETWORK_MODE") ;; esac && if ((${#JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS[@]})); then printf 'Jellyfin startup blocked by recovery dependencies:\n' >&2; printf '  %s\n' "${JELLYFIN_START_BLOCKERS[@]}" >&2; false; fi && docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" up -d && JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" ps -q "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE") && test -n "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID"

Expected successful result: Protected state, external media, named volumes, and actual networking dependencies pass the immediate recheck; exactly one scoped Compose startup runs; and Compose returns the Jellyfin service container ID without deriving its generated name.

If verification fails: Restore every listed protected state, media, volume, or network dependency before retrying. Do not create empty protected or media paths. If dependencies pass, inspect restricted project status and logs without exposing environment values or credentials.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin verification cannot begin until the restored service starts with protected state and separately maintained media attached.

sections.heading: 7. Verify container stability and Jellyfin HTTP service
paragraphs: Required operator action: Verify the Compose-discovered service is running, stable, and healthy when a health check exists. Discover the Jellyfin HTTP endpoint from published 8096/8920 mappings first, host networking second, and a container address only as fallback. Do not log in or expose credentials or API keys.

Verification command: JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE") && test -n "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID" && JELLYFIN_RESTARTS_BEFORE=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID") && sleep 5 && JELLYFIN_RESTARTS_AFTER=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID") && test "$JELLYFIN_RESTARTS_BEFORE" = "$JELLYFIN_RESTARTS_AFTER" && JELLYFIN_HEALTH=$(docker inspect --format '{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{end}}' "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID") && ( test -z "$JELLYFIN_HEALTH" || test "$JELLYFIN_HEALTH" = healthy ) && JELLYFIN_WEB_PUBLICATION=$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --format json | jq -r --arg service "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE" '.[] | select(.Service == $service) | (.Publishers // [])[] | select(.TargetPort == 8096 or .TargetPort == 8920) | [(.TargetPort | tostring), (.PublishedPort | tostring), (.URL // "")] | @tsv' | sort -n | head -n 1) && if test -n "$JELLYFIN_WEB_PUBLICATION"; then IFS=$'\t' read -r JELLYFIN_WEB_TARGET_PORT JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST_PORT JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST <<< "$JELLYFIN_WEB_PUBLICATION"; case "$JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST" in ''|'0.0.0.0'|'::'|'[::]') JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST=127.0.0.1 ;; esac; JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=$JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST; JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT=$JELLYFIN_WEB_HOST_PORT; else JELLYFIN_WEB_TARGET_PORT=$(docker inspect "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].Config.ExposedPorts // {} | keys[] | split("/")[0] | select(. == "8096" or . == "8920")' | sort -n | head -n 1) && test -n "$JELLYFIN_WEB_TARGET_PORT" && if test "$JELLYFIN_NETWORK_MODE" = host; then JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=127.0.0.1; else JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST=$(docker inspect "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].NetworkSettings.Networks | to_entries[] | .value.IPAddress | select(length > 0)' | head -n 1); fi; JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT=$JELLYFIN_WEB_TARGET_PORT; fi && test -n "$JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST" && if test "$JELLYFIN_WEB_TARGET_PORT" = 8920; then JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_URL="https://$JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST:$JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT/System/Info/Public"; JELLYFIN_CURL_TLS=--insecure; else JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_URL="http://$JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_HOST:$JELLYFIN_WEB_ENDPOINT_PORT/System/Info/Public"; JELLYFIN_CURL_TLS=; fi && JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_INFO=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_INFO" && JELLYFIN_HTTP_STATUS=$(curl $JELLYFIN_CURL_TLS --silent --show-error --output "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_INFO" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_URL") && test "$JELLYFIN_HTTP_STATUS" = 200 && jq -e 'type == "object"' "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_INFO" > /dev/null

Expected successful result: The service remains running without restart growth, is healthy when health exists, and the discovered public Jellyfin system-info endpoint returns HTTP 200 with a JSON object. Remapped host ports work and arbitrary 404 responses do not pass.

If verification fails: Check Compose service state, restart causes, health output, published ports, host or container networking, TLS, firewall reachability, and restricted logs. Do not log in, reset passwords, or expose credentials or API keys.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin is not operational while its service is unstable, unhealthy, or its public availability endpoint is unavailable.

sections.heading: 8. Verify Jellyfin recognizes restored application state
paragraphs: Required operator action: Verify safe public server identity/version evidence, confirm the initial setup wizard is not unexpectedly active, prove protected configuration is attached from restored sources, and inspect only narrowly scoped database/configuration initialization failures in restricted logs. Retain manual confirmation for authenticated state.

Verification command: jq -e '(.Version | type == "string" and length > 0) and .StartupWizardCompleted == true' "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_INFO" > /dev/null && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do if test "$classification" = protected-state; then docker inspect "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg source "$source" --arg target "$target" 'any(.[].Mounts[]; .Destination == $target and (.Source == $source or .Name == $source))' > /dev/null; fi; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && JELLYFIN_RECOVERY_LOG=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$JELLYFIN_RECOVERY_LOG" && docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" logs --since 10m --no-color > "$JELLYFIN_RECOVERY_LOG" && if grep -Eiq 'database.*(corrupt|failed)|configuration.*(failed|invalid)|migration.*failed' "$JELLYFIN_RECOVERY_LOG"; then printf '%s\n' 'Restricted Jellyfin logs contain a persistent database or configuration initialization failure.' >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Public JSON contains a Jellyfin version, StartupWizardCompleted is true, every protected-state mount is attached from its expected restored source, and the mode-600 log contains no narrowly matched persistent database or configuration initialization failure.

If verification fails: Stop if first-run setup appears unexpectedly, a protected mount differs, or scoped failure indicators occur. Recheck protected application-state recovery and restricted logs; do not initialize a new server, print unrestricted logs, or expose users, libraries, tokens, or media details.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin cannot be considered restored while it presents first-run setup or fails to recognize protected application state.

sections.heading: 9. Complete manual Jellyfin validation
paragraphs: Required operator action: Manually confirm expected users and access behavior, libraries and their external paths, representative movie or television metadata, successful representative playback with seeking and normal audio/video, recordings when deployed, remote or Nginx Proxy Manager access when configured, hardware transcoding when protected deployment evidence requires it, and scheduled scans and important tasks. Do not require exact media totals without authoritative evidence.

Verification command: printf '%s\n' 'Manual Jellyfin validation required:' '  - expected users and access behavior' '  - expected libraries and external media paths' '  - representative movie or television metadata' '  - representative playback, seeking, audio, and video' '  - expected recordings when deployed' '  - expected remote or proxied access when configured' '  - hardware transcoding when part of the deployment' '  - scheduled library scans and important tasks'

Expected successful result: The operator records every applicable confirmation against protected evidence, including at least one successful representative playback, without treating container status or metadata alone as proof of library correctness.

If verification fails: Keep the specific user, library, path, metadata, playback, recording, proxy, transcoding, or scheduled-task issue as a blocker. Recover missing media only from separately maintained storage; it cannot be reconstructed from Jellyfin metadata or the Docker backup.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Library correctness and playback quality require manual confirmation before Jellyfin recovery is complete.

sections.heading: 10. Confirm Jellyfin recovery is complete
paragraphs: Required operator action: Proceed only after all automatic checks and step 9 confirmations pass. Recheck service stability, the public endpoint, protected configuration attachment, and separately maintained media mounts, then explicitly record complete recovery.

Verification command: test -n "$(docker compose -f "$JELLYFIN_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$JELLYFIN_SERVICE")" && JELLYFIN_FINAL_RESTARTS=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$JELLYFIN_CONTAINER_ID") && test "$JELLYFIN_FINAL_RESTARTS" = "$JELLYFIN_RESTARTS_AFTER" && test "$(curl $JELLYFIN_CURL_TLS --silent --show-error --output /dev/null --write-out '%{http_code}' "$JELLYFIN_PUBLIC_URL")" = 200 && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) jellyfin_state_present "$type" "$source" ;; external-media) jellyfin_media_present "$type" "$source" ;; runtime-support) case "$type" in bind) test -e "$source" && test -r "$source" ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; esac ;; esac || exit 1; done < "$JELLYFIN_MOUNT_REPORT" && printf '%s\n' 'Jellyfin application state has been restored.' 'The separately maintained media library is available.' 'Representative playback has been manually confirmed.' 'Jellyfin recovery is complete.'

Expected successful result: Compose reports Jellyfin running with a stable restart count, the public endpoint responds, protected state remains attached, external media remains mounted, readable, and present, all manual blockers are cleared, and all four completion statements print.

If verification fails: Return to the failed state, media, network, stability, HTTP, first-run, library, playback, proxy, or manual-validation check. Do not declare recovery while protected state is missing, setup is unexpectedly active, media is absent or empty, expected libraries are absent, playback or required proxy access fails, or any blocker remains.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Jellyfin recovery is incomplete until protected application state, separately maintained media, and representative playback are all verified.

entries.title: Home Assistant Recovery
entries.summary: Restore Home Assistant's protected application state and verify that the restored instance is operational.

sections.heading: 1. Locate the Home Assistant Compose project
paragraphs: Required operator action: Open one dedicated Bash recovery shell and keep it open through step 10. Discover Compose definitions beneath /srv/docker, identify services whose resolved service name or image indicates Home Assistant, automatically accept one unique match, and use the constrained candidate list only when multiple valid matches exist. Do not display resolved environment values or use generated container names.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES=$(mktemp) && HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES=$(mktemp) && HOMEASSISTANT_MOUNT_REPORT=$(mktemp) && HOMEASSISTANT_PORT_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES" "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES" "$HOMEASSISTANT_MOUNT_REPORT" "$HOMEASSISTANT_PORT_REPORT" && find /srv/docker -maxdepth 4 -type f \( -name compose.yaml -o -name compose.yml -o -name docker-compose.yaml -o -name docker-compose.yml \) -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d '' candidate; do docker compose -f "$candidate" config --quiet 2> /dev/null && printf '%s\0' "$candidate"; done > "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES" && while IFS= read -r -d '' candidate; do docker compose -f "$candidate" config --format json | jq -r --arg file "$candidate" '.services | to_entries[] | select((.key | ascii_downcase | test("home.?assistant")) or ((.value.image // "") | ascii_downcase | test("home-assistant|homeassistant"))) | [$file, .key] | @tsv'; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_CANDIDATES" > "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES" && test -s "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES" && if test "$(wc -l < "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES")" -eq 1; then IFS=$'	' read -r HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE < "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES"; else nl -ba "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES" >&2; select HOMEASSISTANT_SELECTION in $(seq 1 "$(wc -l < "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES")"); do IFS=$'	' read -r HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE < <(sed -n "${HOMEASSISTANT_SELECTION}p" "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE_CANDIDATES"); test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" && break; done; fi && HOMEASSISTANT_PROJECT=$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r '.name') && test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_PROJECT" && test "$HOMEASSISTANT_PROJECT" != null && docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '.services[$service].volumes[]? | [$service, .type, .source, .target] | @tsv' > "$HOMEASSISTANT_MOUNT_REPORT" && docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '.services[$service].ports[]? | [.target, (.published // ""), (.host_ip // "")] | @tsv' > "$HOMEASSISTANT_PORT_REPORT" && printf 'Compose file: %s
Project: %s
Service: %s
Keep this shell open through step 10.
' "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" "$HOMEASSISTANT_PROJECT" "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE"

Expected successful result: One valid resolved Compose project and Home Assistant service are retained in the same shell, with restricted mount and published-port reports available for later steps and no environment values displayed.

If verification fails: Confirm the protected Compose definition was restored beneath /srv/docker and resolves successfully. If multiple valid candidates exist, repeat only the constrained numeric selection; do not type a Compose path, service name, or container name.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Home Assistant cannot be restored safely without an unambiguous valid Compose service and retained recovery context.

sections.heading: 2. Classify Home Assistant mounts
paragraphs: Required operator action: Classify every Compose-derived mount as protected-state, rebuildable, or runtime-support. Treat /config as protected state, cache and temporary targets as rebuildable, and known host-integration targets such as /run/dbus, /etc/localtime, and /etc/timezone as runtime support. Resolve every ambiguous mount through the constrained choices using protected evidence; do not type paths or arbitrary classifications.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS" && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target; do case "${target,,}" in /config|/config/*) classification=protected-state ;; *cache*|/tmp|/tmp/*) classification=rebuildable ;; /run/dbus|/run/dbus/*|/etc/localtime|/etc/timezone) classification=runtime-support ;; *) printf 'Classify Compose mount source %s at target %s using protected evidence:\n' "$source" "$target"; select classification in protected-state rebuildable runtime-support; do case "$classification" in protected-state|rebuildable|runtime-support) break ;; esac; done ;; esac; printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$service" "$type" "$source" "$target" "$classification" >> "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS"; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_MOUNT_REPORT" && test "$(wc -l < "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS")" -eq "$(wc -l < "$HOMEASSISTANT_MOUNT_REPORT")" && ! grep -Eq $'\t(unresolved|review-required)$' "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS"
Expected successful result: The mode-600 report contains exactly one constrained classification for every resolved mount, and no mount remains unresolved.

If verification fails: Use protected Compose and recovery evidence to repeat the constrained classification. Do not inspect configuration contents, enter free-form infrastructure values, or classify every persistent mount as protected merely because Compose declares it.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Startup safety cannot be established while any mount role is unresolved.

sections.heading: 3. Verify protected Home Assistant state
paragraphs: Required operator action: Before startup, prove every protected-state bind and named volume exists, is readable, and contains bounded evidence of restored Home Assistant state. Empty protected locations block startup. Verify every runtime-support mount exists and is readable; leave rebuildable storage unmodified. Do not assume host UID/GID values or container identities.

Verification command: homeassistant_state_present() { local type=$1 source=$2 mountpoint; case "$type" in bind) test -d "$source" && test -r "$source" && find "$source" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 3 -print -quit | grep -q . ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 && mountpoint=$(docker volume inspect --format '{{.Mountpoint}}' "$source") && test -n "$mountpoint" && sudo test -d "$mountpoint" && sudo test -r "$mountpoint" && sudo find "$mountpoint" -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 3 -print -quit | grep -q . ;; *) false ;; esac; } && homeassistant_runtime_present() { local type=$1 source=$2; case "$type" in bind) test -e "$source" && test -r "$source" ;; volume) docker volume inspect "$source" > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; *) false ;; esac; } && HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_STATE=() && HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_RUNTIME=() && while IFS=$'	' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) homeassistant_state_present "$type" "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_STATE+=("$type:$source") ;; runtime-support) homeassistant_runtime_present "$type" "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_RUNTIME+=("$type:$source") ;; rebuildable) printf 'Rebuildable storage identified: %s -> %s
' "$source" "$target" ;; esac; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS" && if ((${#HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_STATE[@]})); then printf 'Missing or empty protected Home Assistant state:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_STATE[@]}" >&2; false; fi && if ((${#HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_RUNTIME[@]})); then printf 'Unavailable Home Assistant runtime-support mounts:
' >&2; printf '  %s
' "${HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_RUNTIME[@]}" >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Every protected configuration and database location is readable and non-empty by a bounded check, runtime-support mounts are available, rebuildable storage remains distinct, and no filenames or contents are printed.

If verification fails: Restore each missing or empty protected bind or named volume from verified Home Assistant recovery material, or restore the declared runtime-support dependency. Do not create directories or volumes, initialize clean state, hash or fully traverse state, modify configuration, or print filenames.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Home Assistant must not start with missing or empty protected state or unavailable runtime support.

sections.heading: 4. Verify required host dependencies
paragraphs: Required operator action: Derive host devices, privileged mode, and added capabilities only from the selected service's resolved Compose definition. Verify each declared host device source exists and remains accessible. Record privileged and capability declarations without assuming additional hardware or changing host configuration.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT" && docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '.services[$service] | "privileged\t\(.privileged // false)", (.cap_add[]? | "capability\t\(.)"), (.devices[]? | "device\t\(.source)\t\(.target)")' > "$HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT" && HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_DEVICES=() && while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind source target; do test "$kind" != device || test -e "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_DEVICES+=("$source"); done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT" && if ((${#HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_DEVICES[@]})); then printf 'Missing Compose-declared Home Assistant devices:\n' >&2; printf '  %s\n' "${HOMEASSISTANT_MISSING_DEVICES[@]}" >&2; false; fi

Expected successful result: Every device explicitly required by Compose exists, and the restricted report records only non-secret privileged, capability, and device metadata required for the restored service.

If verification fails: Restore or reconnect only the missing Compose-declared device or correct the protected Compose definition from authoritative recovery material. Do not fabricate hardware, alter permissions, add capabilities, or enable privileged mode during verification.
Blocks recovery: Yes when a Compose-declared host dependency is absent. No undeclared hardware is required by this step.

sections.heading: 5. Verify Home Assistant networking
paragraphs: Required operator action: Derive the selected service's actual network mode and networks from resolved Compose metadata. Accept host networking as configured, verify every normal Compose network that will actually be used, and block unsupported none or shared namespace modes. Do not fabricate a default network or create Docker networks.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" && HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '.services[$service].network_mode // ""') && case "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE" in host) : > "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; none) printf '%s
' 'Home Assistant network_mode none cannot provide the required service endpoint.' >&2; false ;; service:*|container:*) printf 'Shared network namespace requires independent recovery: %s
' "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE" >&2; false ;; bridge) printf '%s
' bridge > "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" && docker network inspect bridge > /dev/null 2>&1 ;; '') docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '. as $config | if (($config.services[$service].networks // {}) | length) > 0 then ($config.services[$service].networks | keys[]) as $key | ($config.networks[$key].name // ($config.name + "_" + $key)) else ($config.name + "_default") end' > "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" && while read -r network; do test -z "$network" || docker network inspect "$network" > /dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; *) printf 'Unsupported Home Assistant network mode: %s
' "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE" >&2; false ;; esac
Expected successful result: Host mode records no fabricated Docker network; normal networking records and verifies only networks Compose will attach; every actual required network exists.

If verification fails: Restore the exact missing network or shared networking dependency from protected platform evidence and repeat this check. Do not create a replacement automatically or infer a network from container names.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Home Assistant cannot start until its configured networking semantics and dependencies are restored.

sections.heading: 6. Start the Home Assistant stack
paragraphs: Required operator action: Immediately recheck protected state, runtime-support mounts, and declared host devices. Re-derive the selected service's network mode from the current resolved Compose definition, require it to match step 5, and recheck the saved network report according to that fresh mode before starting only the selected Home Assistant project. Discover the running container through Compose service identity and never use a generated container name.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS=() && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) homeassistant_state_present "$type" "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("state:$source") ;; runtime-support) homeassistant_runtime_present "$type" "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("runtime:$source") ;; esac; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS" && while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind source target; do test "$kind" != device || test -e "$source" || HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("device:$source"); done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT" && HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE=$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" config --format json | jq -r --arg service "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" '.services[$service].network_mode // ""') && if test "$HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE" != "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE"; then HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("network-mode-changed:$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE->$HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE"); fi && case "$HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE" in host) test ! -s "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" || HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("unexpected-host-network") ;; ''|bridge) while read -r network; do test -z "$network" || docker network inspect "$network" > /dev/null 2>&1 || HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("network:$network"); done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_REPORT" ;; none) HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("network-mode:none") ;; service:*|container:*) HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("unverified-shared-network:$HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE") ;; *) HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS+=("unsupported-network-mode:$HOMEASSISTANT_START_NETWORK_MODE") ;; esac && if ((${#HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS[@]})); then printf 'Home Assistant startup blocked by recovery dependencies:\n' >&2; printf '  %s\n' "${HOMEASSISTANT_START_BLOCKERS[@]}" >&2; false; fi && docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" up -d && HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID=$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" ps -q "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE") && test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID"

Expected successful result: Every protected state, runtime, and device dependency passes; the freshly derived network mode matches step 5 and its report recheck passes; exactly one scoped Compose startup runs; and Compose returns the selected service's container ID.

If verification fails: Restore every listed dependency before retrying. Do not create missing state or Docker resources, change Home Assistant configuration, reset authentication, or repeatedly restart the service as a verification technique.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Home Assistant verification cannot begin until the restored service starts with all declared dependencies attached.

sections.heading: 7. Verify container stability and Home Assistant availability
paragraphs: Required operator action: Verify the Compose service remains running, its restart count is stable, and its health check passes when one exists. Discover an endpoint from host networking, a published port targeting 8123, or the container network address as a fallback. Verify Home Assistant's unauthenticated manifest rather than accepting arbitrary HTTP success.

Verification command: test -n "$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE")" && HOMEASSISTANT_RESTARTS_BEFORE=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID") && HOMEASSISTANT_HEALTH=$(docker inspect --format '{{if .State.Health}}{{.State.Health.Status}}{{else}}none{{end}}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID") && case "$HOMEASSISTANT_HEALTH" in none|healthy) ;; *) false ;; esac && HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT= && if test "$HOMEASSISTANT_NETWORK_MODE" = host; then HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:8123; else HOMEASSISTANT_PUBLISHED=$(docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].NetworkSettings.Ports["8123/tcp"][]? | select(.HostPort != null) | [.HostIp, .HostPort] | @tsv' | head -n 1); if test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_PUBLISHED"; then IFS=$'\t' read -r ha_host ha_port <<< "$HOMEASSISTANT_PUBLISHED"; case "$ha_host" in ''|0.0.0.0|::) ha_host=127.0.0.1 ;; esac; HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT="http://$ha_host:$ha_port"; else HOMEASSISTANT_ADDRESS=$(docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -r '.[0].NetworkSettings.Networks | to_entries[] | .value.IPAddress | select(length > 0)' | head -n 1); test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_ADDRESS" && HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT="http://$HOMEASSISTANT_ADDRESS:8123"; fi; fi && test -n "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT" && HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST=$(mktemp) && HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/manifest.json")" = 200 && jq -e '.name == "Home Assistant"' "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" > /dev/null && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/api/discovery_info")" = 200 && jq -e '.version | type == "string" and length > 0' "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" > /dev/null && HOMEASSISTANT_RESTARTS_AFTER=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID") && test "$HOMEASSISTANT_RESTARTS_BEFORE" = "$HOMEASSISTANT_RESTARTS_AFTER"

Expected successful result: Compose reports the selected service running, health is healthy when defined, the restart count remains stable, and a discovered endpoint returns a valid Home Assistant manifest plus restricted discovery metadata containing version information.

If verification fails: Check scoped Compose status, declared networking, health status, and a short restricted diagnostic window that does not expose entity attributes, tokens, passwords, secrets.yaml, or configuration contents. Do not treat redirects, authentication responses, or arbitrary 2xx pages as proof of Home Assistant availability.
Blocks recovery: Yes. A stable running service and Home Assistant-specific endpoint response are required.

sections.heading: 8. Verify restored Home Assistant application state
paragraphs: Required operator action: Verify the unauthenticated onboarding status shows no unexpected first-time setup, the protected configuration remains attached, and the same restricted discovery metadata still provides version information. Use service stability as non-content-revealing evidence that configuration loaded without an initialization failure; do not inspect secrets or private configuration.

Verification command: HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING=$(mktemp) && HOMEASSISTANT_INIT_LOG=$(mktemp) && chmod 600 "$HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING" "$HOMEASSISTANT_INIT_LOG" && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/api/onboarding")" = 200 && jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; .done == true)' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING" > /dev/null && jq -e '.name == "Home Assistant"' "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" > /dev/null && jq -e '.version | type == "string" and length > 0' "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" > /dev/null && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do test "$classification" != protected-state || docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg source "$source" --arg target "$target" 'any(.[0].Mounts[]; .Destination == $target and (.Source == $source or .Name == $source))' > /dev/null; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS" && test -n "$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE")" && docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" logs --since 15m --tail 200 --no-color "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE" > "$HOMEASSISTANT_INIT_LOG" 2>&1 && ! grep -Eiq '(fatal|critical).*(home assistant|initiali[sz]ation)|home assistant (core )?failed to initiali[sz]e|error (loading|validating) (home assistant )?configuration|(home assistant configuration|configuration\.yaml|homeassistant\.config).*(load|validat).*(failed|failure|fatal)|(homeassistant[^ ]*recorder|recorder|sqlite|home assistant database).*(corrupt|malformed|initiali[sz](e|ation).*(failed|failure|fatal)|migration.*(failed|failure|fatal))|database migration.*(failed|failure|fatal)' "$HOMEASSISTANT_INIT_LOG"

Expected successful result: Every onboarding task is complete, protected mounts remain attached, Home Assistant remains running with version evidence, and the restricted recent log window contains no narrowly matched fatal initialization, configuration loading/validation, recorder or database corruption/initialization, or database migration failure. Log contents are not printed.

If verification fails: Stop if onboarding appears, a protected mount is absent, the service is unstable, version evidence is unavailable, or any narrowly matched initialization failure is present. Ordinary warnings, unavailable integrations, and recoverable external-dependency errors do not block this check. Inspect the mode-600 file only through approved secret-safe handling; never print it or expose secrets.yaml, tokens, passwords, entity attributes, or private configuration.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Unexpected first-run onboarding, missing restored configuration, or initialization instability means protected Home Assistant state was not safely recognized.

sections.heading: 9. Complete manual Home Assistant validation
paragraphs: Required operator action: Using the restored operator access, manually confirm the expected dashboards, users, integrations, automations, scripts, scenes, devices, entities, notifications, and representative automation behavior. When an external URL is configured, confirm access through Nginx Proxy Manager. Record exceptions without requiring exact entity counts or restoring dependent external systems in this procedure.

Verification command: printf '%s\n' 'Manual confirmation required: expected dashboards and users are present.' 'Manual confirmation required: expected integrations, automations, scripts, and scenes are present.' 'Manual confirmation required: expected devices, entities, and notifications are present without requiring exact counts.' 'Manual confirmation required: the configured external URL works through Nginx Proxy Manager, when applicable.' 'Manual confirmation required: one representative automation executes correctly.'

Expected successful result: The operator records each applicable confirmation, documents any intentionally unavailable dependent integration separately, and verifies one representative automation without exposing credentials or entity attributes.

If verification fails: Keep the missing dashboard, user, integration, automation, script, scene, device, entity, notification, external-access path, or representative automation as an explicit blocker. Recover dependent services in their own procedures; do not modify configuration merely to make this check pass.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Manual confirmation and successful representative automation are required before Home Assistant recovery is complete.

sections.heading: 10. Confirm Home Assistant recovery is complete
paragraphs: Required operator action: Proceed only after every automatic check and manual confirmation passes. Reconfirm the Compose service, stable restart count, Home Assistant-specific endpoint, protected state, runtime-support mounts, and declared host devices, then explicitly record completion.

Verification command: test -n "$(docker compose -f "$HOMEASSISTANT_COMPOSE_FILE" ps --status running -q "$HOMEASSISTANT_SERVICE")" && HOMEASSISTANT_FINAL_RESTARTS=$(docker inspect --format '{{.RestartCount}}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID") && test "$HOMEASSISTANT_FINAL_RESTARTS" = "$HOMEASSISTANT_RESTARTS_AFTER" && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/manifest.json")" = 200 && jq -e '.name == "Home Assistant"' "$HOMEASSISTANT_MANIFEST" > /dev/null && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/api/discovery_info")" = 200 && jq -e '.version | type == "string" and length > 0' "$HOMEASSISTANT_DISCOVERY" > /dev/null && test "$(curl --silent --show-error --output "$HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ENDPOINT/api/onboarding")" = 200 && jq -e 'all(.[]; .done == true)' "$HOMEASSISTANT_ONBOARDING" > /dev/null && while IFS=$'\t' read -r service type source target classification; do case "$classification" in protected-state) homeassistant_state_present "$type" "$source" ;; runtime-support) homeassistant_runtime_present "$type" "$source" ;; esac && if test "$classification" = protected-state || test "$classification" = runtime-support; then docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg source "$source" --arg target "$target" 'any(.[0].Mounts[]; .Destination == $target and (.Source == $source or .Name == $source))' > /dev/null; fi || exit 1; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_CLASSIFIED_MOUNTS" && while IFS=$'\t' read -r kind source target; do case "$kind" in device) test -e "$source" && docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg source "$source" --arg target "$target" 'any(.[0].HostConfig.Devices[]?; .PathOnHost == $source and .PathInContainer == $target)' > /dev/null ;; privileged) docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg declared "$source" '.[0].HostConfig.Privileged == ($declared == "true")' > /dev/null ;; capability) docker inspect "$HOMEASSISTANT_CONTAINER_ID" | jq -e --arg capability "$source" 'any(.[0].HostConfig.CapAdd[]?; . == $capability)' > /dev/null ;; esac || exit 1; done < "$HOMEASSISTANT_HOST_REPORT" && printf '%s\n' 'Home Assistant application state has been restored.' 'Configuration has been successfully recognized.' 'Representative automation has been manually validated.' 'Home Assistant recovery is complete.'

Expected successful result: The service remains stable, the Home Assistant manifest is available, protected configuration and runtime dependencies remain attached, declared devices remain present, manual blockers are cleared, and all four completion statements print.

If verification fails: Return to the failed state, dependency, networking, stability, endpoint, onboarding, or manual check. Do not declare success while first-run onboarding appears, protected configuration is missing, configuration failed to load, runtime dependencies are absent, expected automations are missing, representative automation fails, or any blocker remains.
Blocks recovery: Yes. Home Assistant recovery is incomplete until restored configuration is recognized and representative automation succeeds.
